Hi Alex —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. As discussed, I’m kicking off the Quality Monitoring (QMon) onboarding work so we can get a minimal guardrail in place before your June model rollout. I’ve attached a short "manifest" that breaks the scope into prioritized activities (prompt sets, eval harness integration, alerting thresholds, canary/rollback rules, and runbook owners).

Top-level asks for you: please confirm the primary integration contact (you or Sarah), and whether the rollout window on your side is the week of Jul 9 (you mentioned July timelines).

Key outcomes we’re aiming for in the initial phase (2–3 weeks):
- Ingest 1 canonical prompt set for each of your three product surfaces (triage, reply-suggest, summary).
- Wire eval harness to your staging dataset for daily regression checks.
- Configure two signal-based alerts (QA drop, hallucination rate) and a canary traffic split (10% blue, 90% green) with automatic rollback trigger on critical regressions.

I’ve cc’d Marissa who will own CS coordination and Monica who will lead the eval integration. Ben (performance/ops) will drop a note with suggested canary rollback snippets so your infra folks can review.

If that scope looks good I’ll open a HubSpot task and share the Drive links.

Best,

Alex/Sarah —

Thanks for the staging info Alex. A few practical integration notes from the eval side so your engineers can prepare:

1) Data contract: we need a CSV export with the following columns (id, prompt_text, reference_summary, surface_tag, created_at). We will never store raw patient identifiers; please ensure anonymization prior to sending.

2) Auth & connectivity: we support S3 presigned URLs or a temporary IAM role. Let us know which you prefer.

3) Eval harness config: we will provide a small YAML that declares the prompt sets, metrics (ROUGE-L, F1 for named-entities, hallucination_flag), and the daily schedule. The initial baseline run will take ~45 minutes for ~10k examples.

4) Regression alerts: Monica suggests a two-tier alarm — warning (delta 5–10%) to a Slack channel for triage, and critical (>10% delta or >3% hallucination) which triggers a PagerDuty alert and the canary rollback policy.

I’ll attach a minimal YAML example to the Drive folder.

—Monica

Quick infra note from my side (canary/rollback snippets):

We recommend implementing the following policy (text your infra can drop into their deployment scripts):

- Canary split: route 10% of qualifying traffic (surface_tag==summary && sensitivity==low) to model:canary.
- Monitor: daily_eval.qa_delta and runtime.safety_violation_rate. Evaluate at 15-minute sliding windows during first 4 hours; then hourly checks.
- Automatic rollback trigger: if (qa_delta >= 10%) OR (safety_violation_rate >= 0.03) sustained for two consecutive 15-minute windows -> execute rollback job: set route to previous_model and notify on-call with runbook link.
- Rollforward policy: after rollback, quarantine canary for 48 hours; require a new baseline eval run passing QA and safety thresholds before reattempt.

I’ve placed snippets in canary-rollback-snippets.txt (attached). Alex — if this aligns with your infra we can share precise LB hooks and a Terraform module to wire the split.

Ben Carter
Principal Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: canary-rollback-snippets.txt
